prs.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
prs.author: Dharit13
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: When SSE reconnection in the StreamableHTTP client exhausts MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS, the waiting caller previously got no signal at all - the pending request just hung forever ('infinite reconnection loop' symptom). Both PRs target exactly this same trigger point (max reconnection attempts exceeded in the reconnection path) and aim to surface a failure to the caller instead of silently returning. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: When SSE reconnection in the StreamableHTTP client exhausts MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS, the waiting caller previously got no signal at all - the pending request just hung forever ('infinite reconnection loop' symptom). Both PRs target exactly this same trigger point (max reconnection attempts exceeded in the reconnection path) and aim to surface a failure to the caller instead of silently returning. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs fix the same trigger (max reconnection attempts exceeded) but via different mechanisms. #2395's diff is fully scoped to `_handle_reconnection`: it builds an `ErrorData`/`JSONRPCError` (a pattern already used elsewhere in this file) and delivers it only to the specific in-flight request via `ctx.read_stream_writer`, so only the affected request fails while the rest of the session keeps working. #3098 instead adds a new `_unwrap_exception` helper to pull a `StreamableHTTPError` out of an anyio exception group and raise it, which would propagate out of the task group and is likely to tear down the whole transport/session rather than just the one affected request; its diff also bundles an unrelated change (`from __future__ import annotations as _annotations` -> `from __future__ import annotations`) that isn't part of the stated fix. #2395's narrower, per-request error-delivery approach also matches the same `ErrorData`/`INTERNAL_ERROR`/`JSONRPCError` convention independently used by #3092 for the non-2xx-response case, making it the more consistent fix to keep.

prs.title: Fix substring matches in WWW-Authenticate parsing
prs.author: Whning0513
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same underlying bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: WWW-Authenticate header parsing used naive substring/regex matching for parameter names and challenge boundaries, causing false matches (e.g. one field name matching as a substring of another, or params from a different auth scheme being picked up). Both fix it by tokenizing the header on top-level commas while respecting quoted strings and backslash escapes. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same underlying bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: WWW-Authenticate header parsing used naive substring/regex matching for parameter names and challenge boundaries, causing false matches (e.g. one field name matching as a substring of another, or params from a different auth scheme being picked up). Both fix it by tokenizing the header on top-level commas while respecting quoted strings and backslash escapes. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both add a quote/escape-aware comma splitter, but #3041's `_split_www_authenticate_segments` + `_extract_bearer_auth_params` re-detects the scheme (partitions each comma-separated segment on its leading space) after every comma, so it correctly isolates only the Bearer challenge's params when a header contains multiple challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm=x, Bearer realm=y, error=z'). #3012's `_iter_www_auth_params` finds only the first space in the whole header and then treats every subsequent comma-delimited chunk as a parameter, so a later scheme token (like a second 'Bearer' or 'Basic') in a multi-challenge header would be swallowed in as if it were a parameter value rather than recognized as a new challenge boundary — a case #3041's per-segment scheme check handles that #3012 does not.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs fix the same trigger (max reconnection attempts exceeded) but via different mechanisms. #2395's diff is fully scoped to `_handle_reconnection`: it builds an `ErrorData`/`JSONRPCError` (a pattern already used elsewhere in this file) and delivers it only to the specific in-flight request via `ctx.read_stream_writer`, so only the affected request fails while the rest of the session keeps working. #3098 instead adds a new `_unwrap_exception` helper to pull a `StreamableHTTPError` out of an anyio exception group and raise it, which would propagate out of the task group and is likely to tear down the whole transport/session rather than just the one affected request; its diff also bundles an unrelated change (`from __future__ import annotations as _annotations` -> `from __future__ import annotations`) that isn't part of the stated fix. #2395's narrower, per-request error-delivery approach also matches the same `ErrorData`/`INTERNAL_ERROR`/`JSONRPCError` convention independently used by #3092 for the non-2xx-response case, making it the more consistent fix to keep.

members.author: Bartok9
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs patch the same conditional in validate_tool_use_result_messages (src/mcp/server/validation.py) where an assistant tool_use message followed by a message with no tool_result blocks at all incorrectly falls through to the tool_use_ids != tool_result_ids comparison, producing a confusing 'ids do not match' error. However, the two PRs resolve it with opposite, mutually exclusive semantics: #2962 adds has_tool_results to the outer guard so the check is skipped entirely and NO error is raised when tool_use isn't followed by a tool_result (its test cites SEP-1577 and regresses against issue #2960, arguing the spec has no requirement that a tool_use must be followed by a tool_result). #3053 keeps the original guard and instead raises a new, more specific ValueError ('tool_use blocks must be followed by matching tool_result blocks') in that same situation - i.e. it still treats the case as invalid, just with a clearer message. clusters.pick_reason: Both add a quote/escape-aware comma splitter, but #3041's `_split_www_authenticate_segments` + `_extract_bearer_auth_params` re-detects the scheme (partitions each comma-separated segment on its leading space) after every comma, so it correctly isolates only the Bearer challenge's params when a header contains multiple challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm=x, Bearer realm=y, error=z'). #3012's `_iter_www_auth_params` finds only the first space in the whole header and then treats every subsequent comma-delimited chunk as a parameter, so a later scheme token (like a second 'Bearer' or 'Basic') in a multi-challenge header would be swallowed in as if it were a parameter value rather than recognized as a new challenge boundary — a case #3041's per-segment scheme check handles that #3012 does not.
